clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the action_schema is the description of actions, the reasons for these actions, and the status of these actions.

example.p: Reasons for action include evolving user requirements, manufacturing problems and difficulties that arise when a product is in use.

sourcecode.body:

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: Action information can be attached to any aspect of product data.

clause.title: supported_item
clause.p:
The supported_item allows for the designation of an action_directive, an action, or an action_method.
This specifies the use of an action_resource.

clause.title: action
clause.p: An action is the identification of the occurrence of an activity and a description of its result.
An action identifies an activity that has taken place, is taking place, or is expected to take place in the future.

An action has a definition that is specified by an action_method.
In particular application domains, terms such as task, process, activity, operation, and event may be synonyms for action.

example.p: Change, distilling, design, a process to drill a hole, and a task such as training someone are examples of actions.

dd.p: the label by which the action is known.
the text that characterizes the action. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
the action_method that specifies the procedure selected to carry out the action and a description of the results of that action.
the identifier that distinguishes the action.

note.p: This attribute is an enhancement to the definition of action using a method that is upwardly compatible with ISO 10303-41:1994.

The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.

dd.p: Each action shall be the identified_item in at most one id_attribute.

clause.title: action_directive
clause.p: An action_directive is an authoritative instrument that provides directions to achieve the specified results.

example.p: ISO Directives Part 3 provides guidance for the development of standards documents within ISO.

dd.p: the label by which the action_directive is known.
the text that characterizes the action_directive. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

an informal description of the results of the analysis that was carried out on the elements of the requests set. The request sets are the versioned_action_requests referenced in the requests attribute.

note.p: The reason that different requests are satisfied by the action_directive could be recorded in this attribute.

dd.p: an informal description of any other pertinent information.
a set of versioned_action_request entity data types that defines the expected results.

clause.title: action_method
clause.p:
An action_method is the definition of an activity. This definition includes the activity’s objectives and effects.
This definition may be the basis for actions or the solution for action requests.

example.p: For the action whose name attribute is ‘serve dinner’, the name attribute of related instance of action_method could be ‘cook by recipe’ or ‘purchase takeout food’.

dd.p: the label by which the action_method is known.
the text that characterizes the action_method. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
an informal description of the effects of the action_method.
an informal description of the objectives of the action_method.

clause.title: action_method_relationship
clause.p:
An action_method_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type action_method and provides an identification and description of this relationship.
The role of action_method_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.
This entity, together with the action_method entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3.
This entity may be used to define a procedural relationship among constituent activities.

dd.p: the label by which the action_method_relationship is known.
the text that characterizes the action_method_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
one of the instances of action_method that is a part of the relationship.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the other instance of action_method that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other this attribute shall be the dependent one.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: action_relationship
clause.p:
An action_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type action and provides an identification and description of this relationship.
The role of action_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the label by which the action_relationship is known.
the text that characterizes the action_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
one of the instances of action that is a part of the relationship.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: action_request_solution
clause.p: An action_request_solution is an association between a versioned_action_request and an action_method that is a potential solution for the request.

dd.p: the action_method that is a potential solution.
the versioned_action_request for which a solution is specified.
the text that characterizes the action_request_solution.

note.p: This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to action_request_solution as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994.

dd.p: the label by which the action_request_solution is known.

note.p: This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to action_request_solution as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994.

dd.p: Each action_request_solution shall be the described_item in at most one description_attribute.
Each action_request_solution shall be the named_item in at most one name_attribute.

clause.p: An action_request_status is the association of a status with a versioned_action_request.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the versioned_action_request to which the status applies.

clause.title: action_resource
clause.p: An action_resource is a thing that is identified as being needed to carry out an action.

dd.p: the label by which the action_resource is known.
the text that characterizes the action_resource. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
a set of supported_items for which the action_resource is used.
the action_resource_type that specifies the sort of action_resource that is being used.

clause.title: action_resource_type
clause.p: An action_resource_type is the identification of the kind of action_resource needed to carry out an action.

example.p: This entity may be used to specify the kind of tool needed to perform a process operation.

dd.p: the label by which the action_resource_type is known.

clause.title: action_status
clause.p:
An action_status is the association of a status with an executed_action.
Information about the date and time may be associated with the action_status through the use of date_assignment, date_and_time_assignment, or time_assignment.

dd.p: the label that provides a user interpretable designation for the level of completion of the action.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

example.p: Terms such as ‘pending’, ‘completed’, or ‘scheduled’ are examples of status.

dd.p: the executed_action to which the status applies.

clause.title: directed_action
clause.p: A directed_action is a type of executed_action that is governed by an action_directive.

example.p: A directed_action could be the inspection of a building as directed by city officials according to the city building codes for earthquake safety. The action is the inspection of the building. The directive is issued by city officials guided by the city building codes. In an application protocol, the building authority may be associated with an organization_assignment. The building codes may be associated with a document_reference.

dd.p: the action_directive that governs the directed_action.

clause.title: directed_action_assignment
clause.p: A directed_action_assignment is an association of a directed_action with product data.

dd.p: the instance of the directed_action entity data that is to be associated with product data.
the object_role that specifies the purpose of the association of the directed_action_assignment with product data.
Each directed_action_assignment shall be item_with_role in at most one role_association.

clause.title: executed_action
clause.p:
An executed_action is a type of action that is completed, partially completed, or just identified. It may but need not have status information associated with it.
The role of executed_action can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.
Status information is associated to executed_action through action_status.

example.p: An executed_action could be to ‘paint the office’ with a status of ‘scheduled’. The action is ‘paint the office’. The status further qualifies the action as ‘planned’, ‘scheduled’, or ‘completed’.

clause.title: versioned_action_request
clause.p:
A versioned_action_request is a specification of a desired result.
The desired result being identified and described may be obtained through one of more action_methods.

an informal description of the reason for the versioned_action_request.
the text that characterizes the versioned_action_request. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

clause.title: versioned_action_request_relationship
clause.p:
A versioned_action_request_relationship is a relationship between two versioned_action_request objects.
Two versioned_action_request objects may be related if they address similar problems.
A versioned_action_request may be a version of a work request. It might be related to a different version of the work request using a versioned_action_request_relationship.

the label by which the versioned_action_request_relationship is known.

clause.title: action_directive_relationship

clause.title: acyclic_action_method_relationship
clause.p: The acyclic_action_method_relationship function determines whether the graph of instances of the entity data type action_method that contains relation as one of its links contains a cycle. This function may be used to evaluate either an action_method_relationship or any of its subtypes.

The function returns TRUE if no cycle has been detected. Otherwise it returns FALSE.
The algorithm of the function is explained in annex E.2.
This function is not used in this schema. It is defined here because other ISO 10303 integrated resources and application protocols that use the action_method_relationship entity include rules that use this function.

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the application_context_schema is the applicable usages of product data. This schema provides a mechanism for application protocols to define a frame of reference or context that applies to particular sets of product data.
This schema also provides a means to identify application protocols.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: The meaningful exchange of product data requires the identification of the application context in which that product data is defined. An application context may have several context elements. Each context element may be referenced by a different set of product data.

clause.title: exchange_identification_context_select
clause.p: The exchange_identification_context_select type allows for the designation of the data types identification_assignment and organization .

clause.title: application_context
clause.p: An application_context, as defined in ISO 10303-1, is a context in which product data is defined and has meaning. An application_context represents various types of information that relate to product data and may affect the meaning and usage of that data.

dd.p: the label by which the application_context is known.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the text that characterizes the application_context.

note.p: The description attribute aids in defining the usage of product data in an application_context.
This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to application_context as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994.

dd.p: the identifier that distinguishes the application_context.

note.p: This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to application_context as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994.

The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the set of instances of the entity data type application_context_element that defines the various aspects of the application_context.
Each application_context shall be the described_item in at most one description_attribute.

note.p: The description_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303.

dd.p: Each application_context shall be the identified_item in at most one id_attribute.

note.p: The id_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303.
A template for constraining the population of the entity data types defined in the basic_attribute_schema is described in annex E.

clause.title: application_context_element
clause.p: An application_context_element is an aspect of an application context that contains information about the context in which product data is defined. This aspect contains information about the conditions in which the product data exists.
An application_context_element may be either a library_context or a product_concept_context, or a product_context, or a product_definition_context.

dd.p: the label by which the application_context_element is known.

example.p: ‘Functional definition’, ‘physical definition’, ‘usage occurrence’, and ‘manufacturable definition’ are examples of names.

dd.p: the application_context of which this application_context_element is a member.

clause.title: application_context_relationship
clause.p:
An application_context_relationship is a relationship between two instances of application_context and provides a description of their relationship.
The role of application_context_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.
Without any further specialization, this relationship does not imply that the product data associated with relating_context are also associated with the related_context.
Relationships represented using this entity may be parent child relationship. Annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity specify whether or not the relationship is directed.
This entity, together with the application_context entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3.

dd.p: the label by which the application_context_relationship is known.
the text that characterizes the application_context_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
one of the instances of application_context that is a part of the relationship.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the other instance of application_context that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other, this attribute shall be the dependent one.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: application_protocol_definition
clause.p: An application_protocol_definition is the identification of an application protocol.

dd.p: the label that provides a user interpretable designation for the level of completion of the application protocol.

example.p: “IS”, “DIS”, “TS” or “CD” are examples of application protocol states.

dd.p: the EXPRESS schema name of the application interpreted model.
the year when the application protocol attained the status given by the status attribute.
the application context of the application protocol.

clause.title: library_context
clause.p: A library_context is a type of application_context_element that defines a context for elements of a library.

The inherited attribute name identifies or characterizes the type of library.
The name attribute can represent the nature of the source of the library, the nature of the contents of the library, or both.

example.p: ‘Dewey Decimal’, ‘ISO 13584 library’, and ‘supplier catalogue’ are examples of type of library.

dd.p: the label that identifies the library.

example.p: ‘ACME self-propelled rocket sleds catalogue’ is an example of a library reference.

clause.title: product_concept_context
clause.p: A product_concept_context is a type of application_context_element that defines a context for a product_concept (see ISO 10303-44).
A product_concept_context represents information that relates to the characterization of potential purchasers of a product. Such information may affect the meaning and usage of the product data.

dd.p: the label that identifies the kind of consumer preferences associated with a product.

example.p: ‘Luxury automobiles’, ‘laptop personal computers’, and ‘budget personal stereos’ are examples of *market_segment_type*s.

clause.title: product_context
clause.p:
A product_context is a type of application_context_element that represents life cycle independent information about a product. This information describes the discipline in which data about the product are created.
Different annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity data type can make use of common values for the attributes of the product_context entity data type in order to establish consistency among schemas that relate to the same types or kinds of products.

example.p: Two annotated EXPRESS schemas that specify product data structures for design and construction of buildings respectively can each constrain the values of the name attribute to be ‘building’, and the discipline_type attribute to be ‘architecture’.

clause.p:
The inherited attribute name identifies a particular industry, subject area, or kind of product for which product data is created or used.
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

example.p: ‘ship’, ‘aircraft’ and ‘building’ are examples of names of product contexts.

dd.p: the label that identifies a particular field of practice involved in creating or using product data.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

example.p: ‘electronics’, ‘engineering’, or ‘architecture’ are examples of discipline types.

clause.title: product_definition_context
clause.p:
A product_definition_context is a type of application_context_element that represents information about the stage in the product life cycle for which a product_definition is created or used.
Different annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity data type can make use of common values for the attributes of the product_definition_context entity data type in order to maintain consistency between schemas that relate to the same or related life-cycle phases.

example.p: Two annotated EXPRESS schemas that specify product data structures for conceptual design and detailed design of process plants respectively can each constrain the values of the name attribute to be ‘conceptual design’ and ‘detailed design’, and the life_cycle_stage attribute to be ‘design’.

clause.p:
The inherited attribute name identifies a subdivision or characterization of a life cycle stage for which product data is created or used.
The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

example.p: ‘required’ and ‘planned’ are examples of names of product definition contexts, used in conjunction with a life cycle stage of ‘thermal analysis’.

dd.p: the label that identifies a stage in the life cycle of a product.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

example.p: A ‘preliminary design’ and ‘manufacturing planning’ are examples of life cycle stages.

clause.title: dependent_product_definition_exchange_context
clause.p: A dependent_product_definition_exchange_context is a type of product_definition_context and is an abstract entity that describes a specific context for exchange.

dd.p: at least one of the entities identification_dependent_product_definition_exchange_context or language_dependent_product_definition_exchange_context shall be specified.

clause.p: An identification_dependent_product_definition_exchange_context is a type of dependent_product_definition_exchange_context that establishes the context of the product_definition exchange.

dd.p: specifies the context of the exchange to be either identification_assignment or organization .

clause.title: language_dependent_product_definition_exchange_context
clause.p: A language_dependent_product_definition_exchange_context is a type of dependent_product_definition_exchange_context that establishes the specified language of the product_definition exchange context.

dd.p: specifies the default language of the exchange context.

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the approval_schema is the description of authorization data. Approval information concerns the acceptance of product data.

example.p: One version of a product may be approved for manufacture whilst another may still be undergoing design.

sourcecode.body:
SCHEMA approval_schema '{iso standard 10303 part(41) version(7) object(1) approval_schema(3)}';
REFERENCE FROM basic_attribute_schema (description_attribute, description_attribute_select, get_description_value, get_role, object_role, role_association, role_select); REFERENCE FROM date_time_schema (date_time_select); REFERENCE FROM person_organization_schema (person_organization_select); REFERENCE FROM support_resource_schema (bag_to_set, label, text);

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: Approval information can be attached to any aspect of product data.

clause.title: approval
clause.p:
An approval is a confirmation of the product data for its intended use. An approval is an incompletely modelled concept and requires population of related entity data types to form a complete approval.
The role of approval can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the type or level of approval in terms of its usage.

example.p: One possible status is ‘released for production’; this explicitly identifies the approved usage. Another possible status is ‘preliminary design completed’; this only implies the approved usage that will depend upon company-specific procedures.

dd.p: the label that provides a user interpretable designation for the level of completion of the approval.

clause.title: approval_date_time
clause.p: An approval_date_time is an association between an approval and a date, time, or date and time.

dd.p: the moment when the dated_approval is given.
the approval with which the date or time is associated.
the object_role that specifies the purpose of the association of the approval_date_time with product data.

note.p: This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to approval_date_time as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994.

dd.p: Each approval_date_time shall be the item_with_role in at most one role_association.

note.p: A template for constraining the population of the entity data types defined in the basic_attribute_schema is described in annex E.

clause.title: approval_person_organization
clause.p: An approval_person_organization is an association between an approval and a given person, organization, or person in the context of an organization.

dd.p: the person or organization playing the given role.
the approval that is affected by the person or organization.
the approval_role that specifies the purpose of the association of the approval with a person or organization.

clause.title: approval_relationship
clause.p:
An approval_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type approval with a description of their relationship.
The role of approval_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.
This entity, together with the approval entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3.

dd.p: the label by which the approval_relationship is known.
the text that characterizes the approval_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
one of the instances of approval that is a part of the relationship.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the other instance of approval that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other, this attribute shall be the dependent one.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: approval_role
clause.p: An approval_role is a definition of a function. An approval_role is an incompletely modelled concept and requires population of related entity data types to form a complete confirmation.

dd.p: the label by which the approval_role is known.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the text that characterizes the approval_role.

note.p: This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to approval_role as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994.

dd.p: Each approval_role shall be the described_item in at most one description_attribute.

note.p: The description_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303.
A template for constraining the population of the entity data types defined in the basic_attribute_schema is described in annex E.

clause.title: approval_status
clause.p: An approval_status specifies the state of an approval.

example.p: ‘Approved’ and ‘disapproved’ are examples of approval_status.

dd.p: the label by which the approval_status is known.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: acyclic_approval_relationship
clause.p: The acyclic_approval_relationship function determines whether the graph of instances of the entity data type approval that contains relation as one of its links contains a cycle. This function may be used to evaluate either a approval_relationship or any of its subtypes.

The function returns TRUE if no cycle has been detected. Otherwise it returns FALSE.
The algorithm of the function is explained in annex E.2.
This function is not used in this schema. It is defined here because other ISO 10303 integrated resources and application protocols that use the approval_relationship entity include rules that use this function.

clause.title: relation
clause.p: (input) the candidate approval_relationship to be checked.

sourcecode.body: relation : approval_relationship

clause.title: relatives
clause.p: (input) the set of instances of the entity data type approval for which the function is searching in the relating_approval parameter of the relation argument.

sourcecode.body: relatives : SET [1:?] OF approval

clause.title: specific_relation
clause.p: (input) the fully qualified name of a subtype of the approval_relationship entity.

sourcecode.body: specific_relation : STRING
x : SET OF approval_relationship;

clause.title: General
clause.p:
The subject of the basic_attribute_schema is the assignment of id, name, description and role attributes to aspects of product data. This schema defines the mechanism to define a value for these attributes and associate it with product data.
The concepts defined in this schema do not provide a generic capability to associate an identification, a name, a description, or a role to product data. They are applied, in order to ensure upward compatibility, in the case where a requirement to add one or more of these kinds of attributes to a particular entity data type has been identified during the revision or amendment process of the standard document in which this entity data type is defined.
The associated entities are defined in ISO 10303-41, ISO 10303-43 and ISO 10303-44.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: The following concepts are supported by this schema:

li.p: the assignment of an identifier to product data;
the assignment of a label to product data;
the assignment of a descriptive text to product data;
the assignment of a role to an association of management type data with other aspects of product data.

clause.p: The assignment of an identifier corresponds to the id_attribute entity data type. The entities to which an identifier may be assigned are specified in the id_attribute_select data type. These entities have a derived attribute id. The corresponding identifier value is provided by the get_id_value function. A constraint ensures that there is at most one instance of id_attribute assigned to an instance of an entity in the id_attribute_select type.

The assignment of a name corresponds to the name_attribute entity data type. The entities to which a name may be assigned are specified in the name_attribute_select data type. These entities have a derived attribute name. The corresponding label value is provided by the get_name_value function. A constraint ensures that there is at most one instance of name_attribute assigned to an instance of an entity in the name_attribute_select type.

The assignment of a descriptive text corresponds to the description_attribute entity data type. The entities to which a description may be assigned are specified in the description_attribute_select data type. These entities have a derived attribute description. The corresponding text value is provided by the get_description_value function. A constraint ensures that there is at most one instance of description_attribute assigned to an instance of an entity in the description_attribute_select type.

The assignment of a role corresponds to the role_association entity data type. The entities to which a role may be assigned are specified in the role_select data type. These entities have a derived attribute role. The corresponding object_role is provided by the get_role function. A constraint ensures that there is at most one instance of role_association assigned to an instance of an entity in the role_select type.

clause.title: description_attribute_select
clause.p: A description_attribute_select specifies those objects that may be assigned a descriptive text.

sourcecode.body: TYPE description_attribute_select = EXTENSIBLE GENERIC_ENTITY SELECT; END_TYPE;

clause.title: generic_attribute_list_select
clause.p: A generic_attribute_list_select specifies those objects that may be assigned a generic attribute list.

sourcecode.body: TYPE generic_attribute_list_select = EXTENSIBLE GENERIC_ENTITY SELECT; END_TYPE;

clause.title: generic_attribute_select
clause.p: A generic_attribute_select specifies those objects that may be assigned a generic attribute.

sourcecode.body: TYPE generic_attribute_select = EXTENSIBLE GENERIC_ENTITY SELECT; END_TYPE;

clause.title: id_attribute_select
clause.p: An id_attribute_select specifies those objects that may be assigned an identifier.

sourcecode.body: TYPE id_attribute_select = EXTENSIBLE GENERIC_ENTITY SELECT; END_TYPE;

clause.title: name_attribute_select
clause.p: A name_attribute_select specifies those objects that may be assigned a name.

sourcecode.body: TYPE name_attribute_select = EXTENSIBLE GENERIC_ENTITY SELECT; END_TYPE;

clause.title: role_select
clause.p: A role_select specifies those objects that may be assigned a role.

sourcecode.body: TYPE role_select = EXTENSIBLE GENERIC_ENTITY SELECT; END_TYPE;

clause.title: aggregate_id_attribute
clause.p:
An aggregate_id_attribute is used for the case where there is more than one product data element for a specific identifier.
This entity provides the capability to add an aggregate id attribute to product data using a method that is upwardly compatible with ISO 10303-41:1994 and ISO 10303-43:1994.

dd.p: the identifier that distinguishes the identified_item.

note.p: The context in which attribute_value is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or be default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the collection of items that are identified.

clause.title: description_attribute
clause.p:
A description_attribute is the assignment of a descriptive text string to product data.
This entity provides the capability to add a description attribute to product data using a method that is upwardly compatible with ISO 10303-41:1994, ISO 10303-43:1994, and ISO 10303-44:1994.

dd.p: the text that characterizes the described_item.
the item that is described.

clause.title: generic_attribute
clause.p:
A generic_attribute is the declaration of a named attribute as a text string to enable it to be associated with product data. This capability shall not be used to replace more specific assignment capabilities if both are available to a specified target.
This entity provides the capability to define a generic attribute associated with product data using a method that is upwardly compatible with ISO 10303-41:1994, ISO 10303-43:1994, and ISO 10303-44:1994.

example.p: A person entity data type instance is included in both generic_attribute_select and name_attribute_select. The name attribute of person is provided for the name value.

dd.p: the label used to name the generic_attribute.
the text that characterizes the generic_attribute.

clause.title: generic_attribute_assignment
clause.p:
A generic_attribute_assignment is the assignment of a generic attribute to element of product data.
This entity provides the capability to add a generic attribute to product data using a method that is upwardly compatible with ISO 10303-41:1994 and ISO 10303-43:1994.

dd.p: the generic_attribute to be associated with the product data.
the item to which the attribute is assigned.

clause.title: generic_attribute_list_assignment
clause.p:
A generic_attribute_list_assignment is the assignment of a named list of generic attributes to element of product data.
This entity data type provides a capability to add a named list of generic attributes to certain product data entity data types using a method that is upwardly compatible with ISO 10303-41:1994, ISO 10303-43:1994, and ISO 10303-44:1994.

dd.p: the label used to name the list of generic attributes.
the list of generic_attributes that are assigned to the element of product data.
the item to which the attributes are assigned.

clause.title: id_attribute
clause.p:
An id_attribute is the assignment of an identifier to product data.
This entity provides the capability to add an id attribute to product data using a method that is upwardly compatible with ISO 10303-41:1994 and ISO 10303-43:1994.

dd.p: the identifier that distinguishes the identified_item.

note.p: The context in which attribute_value is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or be default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the item that is identified.

clause.title: name_attribute
clause.p:
A name_attribute is the assignment of a label by which the product data is known.
This entity provides the capability to add a name attribute to product data using a method that is upwardly compatible with ISO 10303-41:1994 and ISO 10303-44:1994.

dd.p: the label by which the named_item is known.
the item to which the name is applied.

clause.title: object_role
clause.p:
An object_role is a specification of a role for the association of management type data with other aspects of product data and a description of that role.
This entity provides the capability to add a role attribute to an association of management type data with other aspects of product data using a method that is upwardly compatible with ISO 10303-41:1994.

dd.p: the label by which the object_role is known.
the text that characterizes the object_role. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

clause.title: role_association
clause.p:
A role_association is the assignment of an object_role to an association of management type data with other aspects of product data.
This entity data type provides a capability to add a role attribute to certain entity data types that specify associations between product data and administrative or management data. Such entity data types are specified in the management_resources_schema.

dd.p: the object_role that specifies the purpose of the association of the role_association with product data.
the item to which a role is assigned.

clause.p: The get_description_value function accepts an object to which a descriptive text string may be assigned and returns this description if present.

If a description_attribute references the object, the function will return the value of the attribute_value attribute of this description_attribute. Otherwise, the indeterminate value will be returned.

clause.p: (input) the object for which an identifier is determined. This is an input to the function.

id_bag : BAG OF id_attribute := USEDIN(obj, ('BASIC_ATTRIBUTE_SCHEMA.' + 'ID_ATTRIBUTE.') + 'IDENTIFIED_ITEM');

clause.p: The get_aggregate_id_value function accepts an object to which an identifier may be assigned and returns this identifier if present.

If an aggregate_id_attribute references the object, the function will return the value of the attribute_value attribute of this aggregate_id_attribute. Otherwise, the indeterminate value will be returned.

clause.title: obj
clause.p: (input) the object for which an identifier is determined. This is an input to the function.

clause.p: The get_name_value function accepts an object to which a label may be assigned and returns this label if present.
If a name_attribute references the object, the function will return the value of the attribute_value attribute of this name_attribute. Otherwise, the indeterminate value will be returned.

clause.title: obj
clause.p: the object for which a label is determined. This is an input to the function.

clause.p: The get_role function accepts an object to which a role may be assigned and returns this role if present.
If a role_association references the object, the function will return the object_role of the role attribute of this role_association. Otherwise, the indeterminate value will be returned.

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the certification_schema is the definition of certifications. A certification assures and validates product data.

example.p: A material certificate states the chemical composition of one or more physical pieces of material, for example, purchased raw material. The presence of the material certificate removes the need to test the composition of the material; it allows the specified material composition to be accepted as fact without further investigation.
A certified supplier can supply goods that do not require checking.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: Certification information can be attached to any aspect of product data.

clause.title: certification
clause.p:
A certification is an assertion of facts. A certification is an incompletely modeled concept and requires population of related entity data types to form a complete certification.
The role of certification can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the label by which the certification is known.
an informal description of the reason the certification is applied.

example.p: A purpose for material certification could be the fact that certain customers demand material certification for the products that are supplied to them.

dd.p: the certification_type that defines the class of certification that is applied.

clause.title: certification_type
clause.p: A certification_type is the kind of certification granted.

example.p: Suppliers and manufacturers can be certified.

dd.p: the text that characterizes the certification_type.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

example.p: A certification type in an example supply chain is ‘supplier’.

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the contract_schema is the description of contract agreements.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: Contract information may be attached to any aspect of a product data.

clause.title: contract
clause.p:
A contract is a binding agreement. A contract is an incompletely modeled concept and requires population of related entity data types to form a complete contract.
Contracts may be enforceable by law.

dd.p: the label by which the contract is known.
an informal description of the reason for the contract.
the contract‘s type.

clause.title: contract_relationship
clause.p:
A contract_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type contract.
The role of contract_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.
Relationships represented using this entity may be parent child relationship. Annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity specify whether or not the relationship is directed.
This entity, together with the contract entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3.

dd.p: the identifier that distinguishes the contract_relationship.

note.p: The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the label by which the contract_relationship is known.
the text that characterizes the contract_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
one of the instances of contract that is a part of the relationship.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the other instance of contract that is a part of the relationship. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other, this attribute shall be the dependent one.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: contract_type
clause.p: A contract_type is the kind of information that an instance of contract conveys.

example.p: A contract for an organization that is supplying goods to another organization could be ‘fixed’ or ’cost plus’.

dd.p: the text that characterizes the contract_type. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

The function returns TRUE if no cycle has been detected. Otherwise it returns FALSE.
The algorithm of the function is explained in annex E.2.
This function is not used in this schema. It is defined here because other ISO 10303 integrated resources and application protocols that use the contract_relationship entity include rules that use this function.

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the date_time_schema is the definition of dates, both calendar and ordinal, time of day, combinations of date and time of day, and periods of time.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: Any kind of product data may have a date, time, or date and time associated with it.

clause.title: ahead_or_behind
clause.p:
The ahead_or_behind type is used to specify whether a given time is ahead of coordinated universal time, behind coordinated universal time or is coordinated universal time.
Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) is the international time standard. It is the current term for what was commonly referred to as Greenwich Meridian Time (GMT). Zero (0) hours UTC is midnight in Greenwich England, which lies on the zero longitudinal meridian. Coordinated universal time is based on a 24-hour clock; therefore, afternoon hours such as 4 pm are expressed as 16:00 UTC (sixteen hours, zero minutes).

clause.title: date_time_or_event_occurrence
clause.p: The date_time_or_event_occurrence type allows for the designation of a date_time_select or an event_occurrence.

clause.title: date_time_select
clause.p: A date_time_select type allows for the designation of a date, date_and_time, or a local_time.

clause.title: day_in_month_number
clause.p: A day_in_month_number is the position of the specified day in a month.

clause.title: day_in_week_number
clause.p:
A day_in_week_number is the position of the specified day in a week as defined in ISO 8601.
Monday is day number 1, Tuesday is day number 2, Wednesday is day number 3, Thursday is day number 4, Friday is day number 5, Saturday is day number 6, and Sunday is day number 7.

clause.title: day_in_year_number
clause.p: A day_in_year_number is the position of the specified day in a year.

example.p: The 27th day of March is day 86 in years that are not leap years and day 87 in leap years.

clause.title: hour_in_day
clause.p: An hour_in_day is the hour element of a specified time on a 24-hour clock. Midnight shall be represented by the value zero.

example.p: The hour_in_day corresponding to 3 o’clock in the afternoon is 15.

note.p: Although ISO 8601 allows two representations for midnight, 0000 and 2400, this part of ISO 10303 restricts the representation to the first value.

clause.title: minute_in_hour
clause.p: A minute_in_hour is the minute element of a specified time.

clause.title: month_in_year_number
clause.p:
A month_in_year_number is the position of the specified month in a year as defined in ISO 8601.
January is month number 1, February is month number 2, March is month number 3, April is month number 4, May is month number 5, June is month number 6, July is month number 7, August is month number 8, September is month number 9, October is month number 10, November is month number 11, and December is month number 12.

clause.title: second_in_minute
clause.p: A second_in_minute is the position of the specified second in a minute.

clause.title: week_in_year_number
clause.p:
A week_in_year_number is the position of the specified calendar week as defined in ISO 8601.
Week number 1 is the week containing the first Thursday of the year. This is equivalent to saying that week number 1 contains the date 4th January.

clause.title: year_number
clause.p:
A year_number is the year as defined in the Gregorian calendar. The year_number shall be completely and explicitly specified using as many digits as necessary to unambiguously convey the century and year within the century. Truncated year numbers shall not be used.
ISO 8601:1988 defines the Gregorian calendar.

example.p: The year_number corresponding to the first manned landing on the moon is 1969 (not 69).

clause.title: calendar_date
clause.p: A calendar_date is a type of date defined as a day in a month of a year as defined in ISO 8601.

dd.p: the day element of the date.
the month element of the date.
The entity shall define a valid calendar date.

note.p: If the month_component is ‘April’, ‘June’, ‘August’, or ‘November’ the day_component will be between 1 and 30; when the month_component is ‘February’ and the year_component is a leap year the day_component will be between 1 and 29; if the month_component is ‘February’ and the year_component is not a leap year the day_component will be between 1 and 28. Otherwise, the day_component will be between 1 and 31.

clause.title: coordinated_universal_time_offset
clause.p:
A coordinated_universal_time_offset is the oriented offset (specified in hours and possibly minutes) from the coordinated universal time. The offset is defined in ISO 8601 The offset value shall be positive.
Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) is the international time standard. It is the current term for what was commonly referred to as Greenwich Meridian Time (GMT). Zero (0) hours UTC is midnight in Greenwich England, which lies on the zero longitudinal meridian. Coordinated universal time is based on a 24-hour clock; therefore, afternoon hours such as 4 pm are expressed as 16:00 UTC (sixteen hours, zero minutes).
A coordinated_universal_time_offset is used to relate a time to coordinated universal time by an offset (specified in hours and minutes) and a direction.

dd.p: the number of hours by which a time is offset from coordinated universal time.
the number of minutes by which a time is offset from coordinated universal time.
the direction of the offset.
the value of the number of minutes offset used to compute the coordinated_universal_time_offset, either the value of minute_offset or 0.
The hour_offset shall be a positive number, less than 24.
The minute_offset shall be a positive number, less than or equal to 59.

If the value of sense specifies that there is no offset from the Coordinated Universal time, hour_offset and actual_minute_offset shall both be equal to zero. If either hour_offset or actual_minute_offset is different from zero, the value of sense shall specify that there is an offset, either ahead or behind, from the Coordinated Universal time.

clause.title: date
clause.p: A date is the identification of a day or week or month in a year. A date may be a calendar_date or an ordinal_date, or a week_of_year_and_day_date, or a year_month. The date is defined in ISO 8601.

dd.p: the year in which the date occurs.

clause.title: date_and_time
clause.p: A date_and_time is a moment of time on a particular day.

dd.p: the date element of the date time combination.
the time element of the date time combination.

clause.title: date_role
clause.p:
A date_role is a role for a date A date_role is an incompletely modeled concept and requires population related entity data types to form a complete date_role.
A date_role is a role for a date_assignment and a description of that role.

dd.p: the label by which the date_role is known.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the text that characterizes the date_role. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

note.p: This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to date_role as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994.

dd.p: Each date_role shall be the described_item in at most one description_attribute.

note.p: The description_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303.
A template for constraining the population of the entity data types defined in the basic_attribute_schema is described in annex E.

clause.title: date_time_role
clause.p:
A date_time_role is a role for a moment of time on a particular day. A date_time_role is an incompletely modeled concept that requires population of related entity data types to form a complete date_time_role
A date_time_role is a role for a date_and_time_assignment and a description of that role.

dd.p: the label by which the date_time_role is known.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the text that characterizes the date_time_role.

note.p: This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to date_time_role as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994.

dd.p: Each date_time_role shall be the described_item in at most one description_attribute.

note.p: The description_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303.
A template for constraining the population of the entity data types defined in the basic_attribute_schema is described in annex E.

clause.title: event_occurrence
clause.p:
An event_occurrence is the fact of a transition between states at some point in time. The description of the event_occurrrnece can provide an implicit representation of either the state preceeding the event_occurrence or the state after the event_occurrence.
The point in time of the existence may not be known in terms of a calendar date before the event_occurrence actually happens. One reason, why the event_occurrence cannot always be expressed as a calendar date, is that the event_occurrence is not possible to plan, for example a break down of a machine.

example.p: The event_occurrence ‘start of production’ implicitly declares that the before the event_occurrence a product was not in production.

dd.p: the identifier that distinguishes the event_occurrence.

note.p: The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the label by which the event_occurrence is known.
the text that characterizes the event_occurrence. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

clause.title: event_occurrence_context_role
clause.p: An event_occurrence_context_role establishes a context for an event_occurrence_assignment. An event_occurrence is an incompletely modeled concept and requires population of related entity data types to form a complete event_occurrence_context_role

example.p: For the event_occurrence ‘start of production’ the product, for which production starts, is the context for that event_occurrence.

dd.p: the label by which the event_occurrence_context_role is known.
the text that characterizes the event_occurrence_context_role. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

clause.title: event_occurrence_relationship
clause.p:
An event_occurrence_relationship is a relationship between two event_occurrences with a description of their relationship.
The role of event_occurrence_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.
This entity, together with the event_occurrence entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3.

dd.p: the label by which the event_occurrence_relationship is known.
the text that characterizes the event_occurrence_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
one of the instances of event_occurrences that is a part of the relationship.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the other instance of event_occurrence. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other, this attribute shall be the dependent one.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: event_occurrence_role
clause.p: An event_occurrence_role establishes a role for an event_occurrence. An event_occurrence_role is an incompletely modeled concept and requires population of related entity data types to form a complete event_occurrence_role

dd.p: the label by which the event_occurrence_role is known.
the text that characterizes the event_occurrence_role. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

clause.title: local_time
clause.p:
A local_time is an instance of time represented on a 24-hour clock by hour, minute, and second. The instance is expressed in the local time zone and the offset with the coordinate universal time shall be specified. This concept is defined in ISO 8601.
This construct is used to represent a moment of time whereas time_measure represents amounts of time.

dd.p: the number of hours.
the number of minutes. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
the number of seconds. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
the offset of the local time zone to the coordinated universal time.
The entity shall define a valid time. The second_component attribute shall only exist if the minute_component attribute exists.

clause.title: ordinal_date
clause.p: An ordinal_date is a type of date defined as a day of a year. This concept is defined in ISO 8601.

dd.p: the day element of the date.
The day_component shall be between 1 and 365 if the year_component is not a leap year. Otherwise the day_component shall be between 1 and 366.

clause.title: relative_event_occurrence
clause.p: A relative_event_occurrence is a type of event_occurrence that takes place with an offset to an event_occurrence.

example.p: ‘Five days after start of production’ is an example for a relative_event_occurrence, where ‘five days’ is an offset relative to an event_occurrence ‘start of production’.

dd.p: the relative_event_occurrence is defined with respect to the base_event.
the amount of time that passes between the occurrence of the base_event and the relative_event_occurrence. A negative offset specifies that the relative_event_occurrence occurs before the base_event.

clause.title: time_interval
clause.p: A time_interval is the identification of an interval of time. This concept is defined in ISO 8601.

example.p: ‘Strike duration’, ‘delay of production’, and ‘Christmas holidays’ are examples for *time_interval*s.

dd.p: the identifier that distinguishes the time_interval.

note.p: The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the label by which the time_interval is known.
the text that characterizes the time_interval. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

clause.title: time_interval_relationship
clause.p:
A time_interval_relationship is a relationship between two time_intervals with a description of their relationship.
The role of time_interval_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.
This entity, together with the time_interval entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3.

dd.p: the label by which the time_interval_relationship is known.
the text that characterizes the time_interval_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
one of the instances of time_interval that is a part of the relationship.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the other instance of time_interval. If one element of the relationship is dependent upon the other, this attribute shall be the dependent one.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: time_interval_role
clause.p:
A time_interval_role is a role that may be assigned to a time_interval and includes a description of that role.
The assignment of a role to a time_interval is accomplished by the time_interval_assignment entity data type.

dd.p: the label by which the time_interval_role is known.
the text that characterizes the time_interval_role. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: time_interval_with_bounds
clause.p: A time_interval_with_bounds is a type of time_interval. The time_interval_with_bounds is bounded either on one side or both sides. If neither secondary_bound nor duration are specified, the time interval begins at the point in time identified by primary_bound and has no specified end point.

example.p: ‘From 01-01-1999 to 31-12-1999’ is an example for a both side bounded time_interval_with_bounds, ‘from 01-01-2000 on’, and ‘until start of production’ are examples for a one side bounded time_interval_with_bounds.

dd.p: one of the bounds of the time_interval_with_bounds. The value of this attribute need not be specified.
the other bound of the time_interval_with_bounds. The value of this attribute need not be specified.

the time_measure_with_unit that specifies the length of a time_interval_with_bounds. If positive, the time_interval_with_bounds is a lower bounded time_interval_with_bounds, else an upper bounded time_interval_with_bounds. The value of this attribute need not be specified.
Either the primary_bound or the secondary_bound or both shall be specified.
The combination of primary_bound, secondary_bound and duration shall not be specified.
If primary_bound is specified and secondary_bound is not specified and if duration is specified, the duration shall be positive.
If primary_bound is not specified and secondary_bound is specified, duration shall be specified and the duration shall be negative.

clause.title: time_role
clause.p:
A time_role is a definition of a role for a local_time.
The assignment of the role to a local_time is accomplished by the time_assignment entity data type.

dd.p: the label by which the time_role is known.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the text that characterizes the time_role.

note.p: This attribute is an upwardly compatible addition to time_role as specified in ISO 10303-41:1994

dd.p: Each time_role shall be the described_item in at most one description_attribute.

note.p: The description_attribute data type is defined in basic_attribute_schema of this part of ISO 10303.
A template for constraining the population of the entity data types defined in the basic_attribute_schema is described in annex E.

clause.title: week_of_year_and_day_date
clause.p: A week_of_year_and_day_date is a type of date defined by identifying the week within a year and the day within that particular week.

dd.p: the week element of the date.
the day element of the date.
The result of the expression day_component + (7 * week_component) shall be between 1 and 366 if the year_component is a leap year.
The result of the expression day_component + (7 * week_component) shall be between 1 and 365 if the year_component is not a leap year.

clause.title: year_month
clause.p: A year_month is a type of date defined as a month of a year.

dd.p: the month element of the date.

clause.title: General
clause.p: The subject of the document_schema is the citations of formal standards or documents that are outside the domain of this International Standard. These resource constructs are used to reference additional information that is relevant to the description of the product.

example.p: International, national, and organizational standards, catalogues, and tables of engineering data are examples of formal standards or documents.

clause.title: Fundamental concepts and assumptions
clause.p: Product data can include citations of other information sources.

example.p: Heat treatment processes documentation can be specified using the resource constructs that are defined in this schema.

clause.title: product_or_formation_or_definition
clause.p: The product_or_formation_or_definition type allows for the designation of a product, a product_definition, or a product_definition_formation.

clause.title: document
clause.p:
A document is an identification of a collection of information.
The information collected need not be represented in a format conforming to any EXPRESS schema.

example.p: JPEG and HTML files are examples of document.

note.p: This part of ISO 10303 provides several resources to describe documents and to associate them with product data. Annex F.2 provides an explanation about how to describe documents if they are to be considered products.

dd.p: the identifier that distinguishes the document.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

The context in which id is used as a discriminating characteristic can be identified in an annotated Express schema that uses or specializes this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the label by which the document is known.

note.p: The name may include the source of the document.

example.p: An example of the source of a document is “ISO”.

dd.p: the text that characterizes the document. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
the document_type that specifies the sort of data that the document describes.
the set of document_representation_type entities that specifies the way a document is represented.

clause.title: document_product_association
clause.p:
A document_product_association is an association between a document and a product, between a document and a product_definition_formation, or between a document and a product_definition.
The role of document_product_association can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.
The document_product_association may establish an equivalence between the document and the product_definition_formation or between the document and the product of the document and the product_definition. This equivalence will provide a document with the versioning structure found in the product_definition_schema.

dd.p: the label by which the document_product_association is known.
the text that characterizes the document_product_association. The value of the attribute need not be specified.
the instance of document that is part of the association.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

dd.p: the instance of product, product_definition_formation, or product_definition entity data type associated with an instance of document.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: document_relationship
clause.p:
A document_relationship is a relationship between two instances of the entity data type document and provides a description of their relationship.
The role of document_relationship can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.
Relationships represented using this entity may be parent child relationship. Annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity specify whether or not the relationship is directed.
This entity, together with the document entity, is based on the relationship template that is described in annex E.3.

dd.p: the label by which the document_relationship is known.
the text that characterizes the document_relationship. The value of the attribute need not be specified.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

clause.title: document_representation_type
clause.p: A document_representation_type is a specification of the way a document is represented.

dd.p: the label by which the document_representation_type is known.

example.p: ‘Digital’ and ‘physical’ are examples for the name.

dd.p: the document for which the kinds of representation are specified.

clause.title: document_type
clause.p:
A document_type is the kind of data that a formal standard or document may provide information about.
The applicable values of document_type can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or by default, in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

example.p: ‘Material’, ‘surface finish’, and ‘heat treatment process’ are all pieces of data that can be described implicitly, by reference to other documents (such as standards documents), rather than explicitly every time they are used.

dd.p: the name of the kind of data contained in a document.

example.p: ‘Material description’ is an example of product_data_type that characterizes the information provided by a standards document for material.

clause.title: document_usage_constraint
clause.p:
A document_usage_constraint is an identification of a specific subject area or aspect from within a document and gives the relevant information or text that applies. The semantics of the reference can be found in the document itself.
This entity could be used to identify the clause of a document and the content or portions of the content in that clause that are relevant.

dd.p: the document in which the subject_element originates.

note.p: The inverse of this relationship is used to define multiple elements of a document.

dd.p: the name of an element of the source.
the label that conveys a specific value of the subject_element present in the source

example.p: For references to a ‘surface finish’ source the subject_element may be a ‘Clause 2.1 surface imperfection’ and its associated subject_element_value may be ‘no visible imperfections’, ‘no more than two imperfections that are more than 0.06 inch diameter within any given square inch of surface area’, or ‘no imperfections under 10 times magnification’.

clause.title: document_with_class
clause.p: A document_with_class is a type of document for which a classification is specified.

example.p: A surface finish document may be identified by various classes, class A, class B, and class C. Each class of surface finish specifies various allowances for imperfections in the surface finish. Class A may require no visible imperfections, class B may require no more than two imperfections that are more than 0.06 inch diameter within any given square inch of surface area, and class C may require no imperfections under 10 times magnification.

dd.p: the identification of the data classification to which the document belongs.

note.p: The meaning of this attribute can be defined in the annotated EXPRESS schemas that use or specialize this entity, or in an agreement of common understanding between the partners sharing this information.

example.p: The value of this attribute would be ‘A’, ‘B’ or ‘C’ in the previous example.

The algorithm of the function is explained in annex E.2.
